beats.note: Guido van Rossum named it after Monty Python's Flying Circus, a BBC comedy series from the 1970s. The official Python FAQ says so directly.
He was looking for a hobby programming project to keep him occupied in the week around Christmas, as he wrote in his 1996 foreword to Programming Python.

beats.text: A working title, chosen in an irreverent mood.
beats.note: He wanted a name that was short, unique and slightly mysterious. He was reading the scripts of the show at the time.

beats.text: It descended from a teaching language.
beats.note: ABC was built by a group at CWI in the Netherlands, where van Rossum had worked. He says ABC gave him the key inspiration for Python.

beats.name: alt.sources
beats.role: The Usenet newsgroup where van Rossum first released Python to the world, just over a year after he began.

beats.text: A holiday hobby, named after a comedy series.
